s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: CPI measures consumer or retail prices and is associated with NSO.
IIP measures industrial output and covers mining, manufacturing and electricity.
IIP measures wholesale prices and is associated with the Office of Economic Adviser.
WPI measures wholesale prices and is associated with the Office of Economic Adviser.
x: Option C is incorrect: IIP measures industrial output (mining, manufacturing, electricity) and is compiled by the NSO. Wholesale prices are WPI, compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser.

s: What does the WPI measure?
x: WPI tracks wholesale prices; CPI tracks retail prices and IIP industrial output.

s: Who compiles the Wholesale Price Index in India?
x: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser; CPI and IIP are compiled by the NSO.

s: Which of the following is INCORRECT?
o: The NSO compiles CPI-Rural and CPI-Urban.
CPI-Combined is the RBI's inflation-target measure.
CPI-IW is compiled by the NSO.
x: CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau; the NSO compiles CPI-Rural, CPI-Urban and CPI-Combined.

s: Which index measures food inflation in India?
o: Wholesale Price Index - Primary Articles only
x: Food inflation is measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), which has 10 sub-groups such as cereals, pulses, vegetables and milk. WPI primary articles is a wholesale measure, CPI-IW is for industrial workers' DA, and IIP measures industrial output, not prices.

s: The CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) in India is published by which organisation?
o: National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
x: The CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

s: What is the current base year of the new CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) series?
x: The new CPI series uses 2024 as its base year and was introduced from the earlier 2012-based series.

s: The current Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is compiled by which body and with which base year?
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; base 2011-12
x:
WPI base revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23 in 2026 — now 2022-23 (Praveen CA360 June 2026; PMF Lens 2026-06-07)
WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry); its base was 2011-12 until 2026 (now 2022-23, 957 items).

s: Which institution publishes national income and GDP estimates in India?
o: State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
x: National income and GDP estimates are published by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; earlier this was done by the CSO.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the uses of price indices?
o: CPI is used for revising dearness allowance
The GDP deflator is used for industrial workers' dearness allowance
WPI is used for contract escalation
WPI is used for industrial analysis
x: Industrial workers' dearness allowance uses CPI-IW, not the GDP deflator; CPI is used for DA and WPI for contract escalation and industrial analysis.

s: How many items does the new WPI series contain?
x: The new WPI series has 957 items, against 697 in the earlier series; its weights are based on Gross Value of Output.

s: Which index is regarded as the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy?
x: The GDP deflator is the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy, including services.

s: Which group carries the largest weight (about 64%) in WPI?
x: Manufactured products carry about 64% weight in WPI, which covers goods only.

s: CPI-AL and CPI-RL are compiled on which current base year?
x: Since June 2025 the Labour Bureau's CPI-AL and CPI-RL use base 2019 (earlier 1986-87).

s: Where is the Labour Bureau, which compiles CPI-IW, headquartered?
x: The Labour Bureau, set up in 1920 under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is at Chandigarh.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Labour Bureau index?
x: CPI-UNME (Urban Non-Manual Employees) is the odd one out; CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL are Labour Bureau series.

s: What is the weight of food and beverages in the new CPI (base 2024)?
x: Food and beverages carry 36.75% in the new CPI; the 2012 series had about 46%.

s: The new CPI series (base 2024) has how many divisions under COICOP 2018?
x: The new CPI has 12 divisions under COICOP 2018, against 6 groups earlier.

s: What does the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measure?
x: IIP measures industrial output, not prices; it is released by NSO.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Index) - List-II (Current base year)
A. CPI-Combined - 1. 2016
B. CPI-IW - 2. 2019
C. CPI-AL - 3. 2024
D. WPI - 4. 2011-12
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x:
WPI base revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23 in 2026 — now 2022-23 (Praveen CA360 June 2026)
CPI-Combined is on base 2024, CPI-IW 2016, CPI-AL 2019; WPI was on 2011-12 (now 2022-23).

s: How many items does the new CPI series (base 2024) cover?
x: The new CPI has 358 items (308 goods, 50 services) in 12 COICOP divisions.

s: In which year was the Labour Bureau, which compiles CPI-IW, established?
x: The Labour Bureau was set up in 1920; it is based in Chandigarh.

s: Under which Ministry does the Labour Bureau function?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
x: The Labour Bureau is under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

s: How many items did the WPI series with base 2011-12 cover?
x: The 2011-12 WPI had 697 items (564 manufactured); the new 2022-23 series has 957.

s: Alongside which new index will the WPI (base 2022-23) run for five years before the WPI is phased out?
x: The new WPI runs with a new Producer Price Index for 5 years, after which the WPI is phased out.

s: On what basis are the weights of the new WPI (base 2022-23) fixed?
x: The new WPI series uses weights based on Gross Value of Output.

s: When was the first data of the new CPI series (base 2024) released?
x: The first release of the base-2024 CPI came on 12 February 2026, for January 2026.

s: How many online platforms were added for price collection in the new CPI (base 2024)?
x: The new CPI added 12 online platforms and rural house rent (February 2026).

s: For whom is CPI-IW mainly used to determine the dearness allowance?
x: CPI-IW is used for determining dearness allowance for industrial workers.

s: How is the GDP deflator calculated?
o: Real GDP multiplied by nominal GDP divided by 100
Nominal GDP divided by real GDP multiplied by 100
Nominal GDP minus real GDP divided by 100
Real GDP divided by nominal GDP multiplied by 100
x: GDP deflator equals nominal GDP divided by real GDP, multiplied by 100. A rise in the deflator reduces the purchasing power of money.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. WPI covers both goods and services.
2. CPI covers both goods and services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CPI measures retail prices of goods and services; WPI measures first-point bulk prices of goods only.

s: A rise in the GDP deflator, other things remaining the same, indicates a reduction in which of the following?
x: An increase in the GDP deflator reflects a rise in the general price level and therefore reduces the purchasing power of money.

s: Which index measures prices at the first-point bulk (wholesale) stage?
x: WPI measures wholesale, first-point bulk prices; CPI measures retail prices.

s:
Consider the following statements about the weights in price indices:
1. Food has a bigger weight in CPI than in WPI.
2. Manufactured goods carry the biggest weight in WPI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Food carries more weight in CPI than in WPI, while manufactured goods (64.23%) carry the biggest weight in WPI.

s: Before the adoption of CPI (Combined) by the RBI in April 2014, India used which index as the headline inflation measure?
x: WPI was earlier used as India's headline inflation measure. The RBI adopted CPI (Combined) as its key measure in April 2014 following the Urjit Patel Committee framework.

s: On whose committee's framework did the RBI adopt CPI (Combined) as the headline measure in April 2014?
x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) made CPI the nominal anchor under flexible inflation targeting.

s: Who headed the working group on WPI revision to base 2011-12?
x: Saumitra Chaudhuri's group (set up March 2012) gave the 2011-12 base; Abhijit Sen's gave 2004-05.

s: Who headed the working group for the WPI base 2022-23?
x: Ramesh Chand of NITI Aayog led the working group for the 2022-23 WPI base (2025).

s: Which base year of the WPI did the Abhijit Sen working group recommend?
x: The Abhijit Sen working group (report May 2008) gave the 2004-05 WPI base; Saumitra Chaudhuri gave 2011-12.

s: Which of the following would generally reduce cost-push inflationary pressure in India?
o: A permanent fall in input costs
x: A fall in input costs reduces cost-push pressure, whereas hoarding, MSP increases and inflation expectations add to inflation.

s: What is inflation caused by a sharp fall in supply while demand stays the same, from structural shortages, called?
x: Bottleneck inflation arises from structural supply shortages (farm productivity, storage, distribution) and is hard for government to tackle.

s: What is inflation caused by strong export demand draining domestic supply called?
x: Export-led inflation occurs when strong export demand drains domestic supply.

s: Which of the following does NOT cause demand-pull inflation?
x: Demand-pull comes from expansionary policy, fiscal stimulus and public spending; rising interest rates do not cause it.

s: A rise in wages, raw material costs and fuel prices leads to which type of inflation?
x: Cost-push inflation results from rising input costs such as wages, raw materials, fuel and a falling rupee.

s: Which type of inflation arises when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply at the full-employment level of output?
x: When demand runs above full-employment output (an inflationary gap), prices are pulled up: demand-pull inflation.

s: Which type of inflation is described as 'too much money chasing too few goods'?
x: Demand-pull inflation comes from excess demand: too much money chasing too few goods.

s: Which of the following generally mitigates, rather than causes, supply-side inflation in India?
x: Monsoon failure, El Nino, costlier crude and rupee depreciation create supply shocks; better storage and distribution efficiency eases them.

s: What is the dominant cause of inflation in India?
x: Supply shocks – erratic monsoon, El Nino, costlier crude and rupee depreciation – are the dominant cause of inflation in India.

s: The Brent crude oil benchmark comes from which region?
x: Brent is the North Sea benchmark; WTI and Dubai are the other two main benchmarks.

s:
Consider the following statements about inflation in India:
1. MSP hikes and hoarding add to inflation.
2. Inflation expectations can feed inflation.
3. Better storage and distribution efficiency worsens supply shocks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: MSP hikes, hoarding and expectations add to inflation; better storage and distribution ease supply shocks, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main crude oil benchmarks?
x: The three main crude benchmarks are Brent, WTI and Dubai.

s: What is inflation returning after a period of deflation, seen as a sign of recovery, called?
x: Reflation is inflation returning after deflation; a falling but positive inflation rate is disinflation.

s: What is a lasting fall in the general price level called?
x: Deflation is a fall in the price level (negative inflation); disinflation is only a fall in the inflation rate, which stays positive.

s: What is inflation running below 3% a year called?
x: Creeping inflation is below 3%; walking inflation is about 3-10%, and galloping inflation precedes hyperinflation.

s: A fall in the inflation rate from 3% to 2% is an example of which of the following?
x: Disinflation is a fall in the rate of inflation that stays positive; prices still rise, only more slowly.

s: Walking (trotting) inflation refers to an annual rate of about how much?
x: Walking inflation is about 3-10% a year; creeping inflation is below 3%.

s:
Arrange the following types of inflation in ascending order of their speed:
1. Galloping inflation
2. Creeping inflation
3. Hyperinflation
4. Walking inflation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Creeping (below 3%) is slowest, then walking (3-10%), then galloping, and hyperinflation is the most severe.

s: What is inflation in only a few commodities, such as food, while overall inflation remains low, known as?
x: Skewflation describes a situation in which prices rise sharply in a few items while prices of other items remain stable and overall inflation is low.

s: What is inflation accompanied by slow growth and unemployment called?
x: Stagflation combines inflation with slow growth and unemployment.

s: Stagflation refers to inflation accompanied by which of the following?
o: A sustained rise in productive capacity
Slow growth and falling industrial output
x: Stagflation is inflation combined with falling industrial output and slow growth; higher government spending can add the inflationary pressure.

s:
Consider the following statements about factors behind stagflation in India:
1. Inflation from higher government spending
2. A fall in industrial production and slow growth
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Stagflation combines inflation (e.g. from higher government spending) with falling industrial production and slow growth.

s: Which of the following describes inflation-indexed bonds?
o: Only the coupon rate is fixed permanently, irrespective of inflation
Repayment is linked exclusively to the exchange rate
The principal is linked to the stock-market index alone
The principal and/or interest is linked to an inflation index
x: In inflation-indexed bonds, the principal and/or interest payments are linked to an inflation index, protecting the investor’s real return.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Monetary measure — sale of securities through open market operations
Fiscal measure — release of onion buffer stocks by NCCF
Supply-side measure — increase in cash reserve ratio
Monetary measure — reduction of indirect taxes on essential goods
x: Sale of securities through open market operations is a monetary measure. Buffer-stock release is supply-side, while taxes and government spending are fiscal instruments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about supply-side measures against food inflation?
o: NCCF and NAFED released onion from the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer
Bharat Atta, Rice and Dal are sold through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar
Pulses and onions are held in the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer
Under OMSS (Domestic), FCI sells pulses and onions at fixed prices
x: Under OMSS, FCI sells wheat and rice; pulses and onions belong to the PSF buffer.

s: What is the main limitation of the repo rate in controlling inflation?
o: Cannot directly resolve supply shocks such as onion or crude-oil price spikes
Can be changed only by the Union Government
Acts only on the supply side
x: The repo rate works on aggregate demand and liquidity, so it cannot directly remove supply shocks like onion or crude-oil price rises.

s: Who heads the State-level Price Monitoring Committee in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Chief Secretary heads AP's State-level Price Monitoring Committee; the DES monitors 8 essential commodities daily.

s: What does the FCI sell under OMSS (Domestic)?
x: OMSS (Domestic) is the FCI's sale of wheat and rice; pulses and onions belong to the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer.

s: Of which commodities does the Price Stabilisation Fund maintain a buffer?
x: The PSF holds a buffer of pulses and onions; wheat and rice are sold under OMSS by the FCI.

s: With what export duty was India's onion export ban lifted on 4 May 2024?
x: The ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 with a 40% duty and US$550 MEP; the duty was cut to 20% on 13 September 2024.

s: What do inflation-indexed bonds mainly offer the government?
o: Protection of investors' nominal return only
Higher interest costs during low inflation
Cheaper borrowing when credible on inflation
x: For government, IIBs give cheaper borrowing when it is credible on inflation and signal commitment to low inflation.

s: What do inflation-indexed bonds mainly provide to investors?
o: A fixed nominal coupon unaffected by prices
x: IIBs link principal and/or interest to an inflation index, protecting the investor's real return.

s: At what price per kg was Bharat Chana Dal sold from July 2023?
x: Bharat Chana Dal was sold at ₹60 a kg from July 2023 through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.

s: Which pulse was later added to the Bharat Dal initiative after chana dal?
x: Bharat Dal began with chana dal and was later extended to moong dal.

s: What was the RBI's repo rate in August 2026?
x: The repo rate stood at 5.25% in August 2026, with a hike expected in October.

s: On 13 September 2024, along with removing the minimum export price, to what level was the export duty on onion cut?
x: On 13 September 2024 the MEP was removed and the onion export duty was cut from 40% to 20%.

s: How many essential commodities does Andhra Pradesh's Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES) monitor daily?
x: AP's DES monitors 8 essential commodities daily.

s: Which commodities were added in February 2025 to the list monitored daily by Andhra Pradesh's DES?
x: Groundnut and palm oil were added to the DES daily watch list in February 2025.

s: In which year did the Reserve Bank of India issue Inflation-Indexed Bonds?
x: The RBI issued Inflation-Indexed Bonds in 2013.

s: Why is food inflation considered regressive?
o: Food inflation benefits fixed-income households most
Food forms a relatively large share of the expenditure of poorer households
Food is excluded from the CPI basket
Food prices are unaffected by supply shocks
x: Food inflation is regressive because poorer households spend a larger share of their income on food. Food and beverages account for approximately 37 per cent of the CPI basket.

s: Deflation can initiate a deflationary spiral because it may lead to which sequence?
o: Postponed purchases, lower profits, higher unemployment and a heavier real debt burden
Immediate purchases, higher profits, lower unemployment and lighter real debt
Higher wages, greater demand, rising output and lower real debt
Higher inflation expectations, increased exports and full employment
x: During deflation, consumers may postpone purchases, causing profits and production to fall; unemployment can rise and the real burden of debt increases.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the distributional effects of inflation?
o: Debtors may gain as the real value of repayment falls
Creditors may lose as money received buys less
Fixed-income groups such as pensioners are automatically protected
Holders of real assets may gain from rising prices
x: Fixed-income groups are generally vulnerable to inflation unless their incomes are adjusted; debtors and real-asset holders may gain while creditors may lose.

s: What is the cost to firms of repeatedly re-pricing goods during inflation called?
x: Menu costs are the costs of repeated re-pricing during inflation.

s: What happens to the purchasing power of money during deflation?
x: When prices fall, each unit of money buys more, so purchasing power rises.

s: Headline inflation is more volatile than core inflation mainly because it includes which of the following?
x: Headline inflation includes food and energy prices, which swing sharply; core inflation leaves them out and is more stable.

s: Food inflation in India is measured by the Consumer Food Price Index, which has how many sub-groups?
x: The CFPI has 10 sub-groups, including cereals, pulses, vegetables, milk and spices.

s: Which measure reflects the underlying long-run trend of inflation, ignoring short-term swings?
x: Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel, so it shows the underlying trend and is more stable.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Headline inflation – Excludes volatile food and fuel
Core inflation – Includes food and energy
x: CPI tracks retail prices; headline inflation includes food and energy, core excludes them, and WPI tracks wholesale goods.

s: What was the relative order of food, headline and core inflation in May 2026?
x: In May 2026, food inflation was 4.85%, headline inflation was 3.93% and core inflation was 3.73%, giving the order Food > Headline > Core.

s: When did the first breach of the 4% CPI inflation target in the new series occur?
x: Headline CPI inflation reached 4.38% in June 2026, marking the first breach of the 4% target.

s: Which explanation was given for WPI inflation being far above CPI inflation in June and July 2026?
o: The inclusion of services in the WPI basket
Higher fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict
A change in the CPI base year alone
A sharp fall in manufactured-goods prices due to domestic oversupply
x: WPI inflation was 9.87% in June and 9.78% in July 2026, far above CPI inflation mainly because of fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict.

s: Which of the following pairs about inflation in May 2026 is correctly matched?
o: Consecutive months AP stayed above the national rate – three
x: AP's retail inflation was 4.9% against India's 3.9% in May 2026, and AP stayed above the national rate for five consecutive months.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's inflation in 2025:
1. CPI inflation was 2.2%, a 12-year low.
2. Food inflation was -0.2%, the first food deflation since 2014.
3. Food inflation was higher than headline inflation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: In 2025 CPI was 2.2% and food -0.2%, so food was below headline (order Core > Headline > Food).

s: What was the order of food, headline and core inflation in the year 2025?
x: In 2025 food inflation was negative (-0.2%), so the order was Core > Headline > Food, unlike 2023-24 and May 2026.

s: What was India's CPI inflation in October 2025, the lowest in the 2012 series?
x: CPI inflation fell to 0.3% in October 2025, the lowest in the 2012-base series.

s: At what level did CPI inflation touch a 20-month high in August 2026?
x: Headline CPI rose to 4.8% in August 2026, a 20-month high.

s: What was WPI inflation on the new 2022-23 base in June 2026?
x: WPI inflation was 9.87% in June 2026, far above CPI because of fuel costs from the West Asia conflict.

s: What does the Phillips curve, associated with A.W. Phillips, depict?
o: An inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment
The relationship between tax rates and tax revenue
An inverted-U relationship between income inequality and per capita income
The cumulative share of income received by cumulative shares of population
x: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relation between inflation and unemployment. Tax rate versus revenue is the Laffer curve; the inverted-U of inequality against income is the Kuznets curve; and cumulative population against cumulative income is the Lorenz curve.

s: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, what is the inflation target retained for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031?
o: 2% core CPI with a band of +/- 2%
x: The Centre, with the RBI, retained the target of 4% CPI-Combined inflation with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e. 2-6%) for 2026-2031 by Gazette notification. WPI and core CPI are not the target index, and 6% is the upper limit of the band, not the target.

s: Under the RBI Act, 1934 (amended 2016), which Section requires a report when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters?
x: Section 45ZN requires the report; Section 45ZA deals with target-setting and Section 45ZB with the MPC.

s: Under the RBI Act, which Section provides for a six-member Monetary Policy Committee?
x: Section 45ZB sets up the six-member MPC; 45ZA covers target-setting and 45ZN the breach report.

s: In which year was Section 45ZN of the RBI Act first invoked?
x: Section 45ZN, requiring a report after three consecutive quarters of band breach, was first invoked in 2022.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about flexible inflation targeting in India?
o: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement was signed in February 2015
x: The target is 4% with a 2-6% band; 6% is only the upper limit, not the target.

s: In which year was the RBI Act, 1934 amended to give flexible inflation targeting a statutory basis?
x: The 2016 amendment of the RBI Act set up the MPC and made flexible inflation targeting statutory.

s: Which Section of the RBI Act provides for the Centre, in consultation with the RBI, to set the inflation target every five years?
x: Section 45ZA deals with target-setting; 45ZB is the six-member MPC and 45ZN the report on a breach.

s: After flexible inflation targeting was adopted, average CPI inflation fell from 6.8% (2012-16) to about what level?
x: Average CPI inflation came down from 6.8% to about 4.9% under flexible inflation targeting.

s: When was the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI signed?
x: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement was signed in February 2015; it led to the 2016 RBI Act amendment.

s: Who established an inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958?
x: A.W. Phillips established the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation (the Phillips curve) in 1958.

s: According to Friedman, what is the shape of the long-run Phillips curve?
x: Friedman held the long-run Phillips curve to be vertical, implying no lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment.

s: Why has the Phillips curve observed in India during 2012-2026 been described as relatively flat?
o: The Reserve Bank of India fixes all wages
The formal workforce has complete wage flexibility
Around 92% of workers are informal and have weak wage-bargaining power
Food prices are excluded from the CPI
x: India’s relatively flat Phillips curve is linked to the large informal workforce, estimated at about 92%, whose weak wage-bargaining power prevents wages from responding strongly to output changes.

s: In the original Phillips curve, what does lower unemployment come with?
x: Phillips (1958) found an inverse relation: lower unemployment goes with higher (wage) inflation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Wealth tax was a direct tax on net wealth, abolished in 2015
Capital gains tax is a direct tax on profit from selling a capital asset
Gift tax was a direct tax on property received without consideration
Customs duty is a direct tax on imports and exports
x: Customs duty is an indirect tax on imports and exports.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indirect taxes are generally non-inflationary.
2. Direct taxes are generally non-inflationary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Direct taxes are generally non-inflationary, while indirect taxes raise prices because their burden is built into prices.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the shifting of tax burden?
o: The burden of GST is generally shifted through prices
Property tax is a direct tax
The burden of property tax can be shifted through prices
x: Property tax is a direct tax and its burden cannot be shifted through prices; GST, an indirect tax, is passed on through prices.

s: On what is corporation tax in India levied?
x: The base of corporation tax is the net profit of companies.

s: What is moving the burden of a tax forward to consumers or backward to suppliers called?
x: This is tax shifting; impact is on whom the tax is first imposed and incidence is on whom it finally falls.

s: Which of the following is an indirect tax?
x: VAT is an indirect tax passed on to buyers, like excise, service tax and sales tax.

s: How is the securities transaction tax (STT), collected by the stock exchange, classified?
x: STT is a direct tax though collected by the exchange; it came from 1 October 2004.

s: The person who finally bears the burden of a tax is said to bear which of the following?
x: Impact is on whom the tax is first imposed; incidence is who finally bears it.

s: Direct taxes in India are administered by the CBDT. Which body administers indirect taxes?
x: Direct taxes are administered by the CBDT and indirect taxes by the CBIC.

s: Why are wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty called 'paper taxes'?
o: Were levied only on paper industries
x: These direct taxes never yielded much revenue, hence the name 'paper taxes'.

s: If the demand for a commodity is perfectly inelastic, who bears the full burden of an indirect tax imposed on it?
x: With zero elasticity buyers do not cut purchases, so the price rises by the full tax and the incidence falls on the consumer.

s: Which of the following indirect taxes was subsumed in GST from 1 July 2017?
x: Service tax was subsumed in GST; corporation tax and STT are direct taxes and basic customs duty stays outside GST.

s: Under which Act is customs duty levied on imports and exports in India?
x: Customs duty on imports and exports is levied under the Customs Act, 1962.

s: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a tax with its taxable event?
o: Customs — manufacture of goods within India
Sales tax or VAT — sale of goods
Service tax — supply of goods only
x: The taxable event for sales tax or VAT is the sale of goods. Manufacture attracts central excise, import or export attracts customs, and provision of service attracts service tax.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Income tax – Value added at each stage
Corporation tax – Company income or profit
VAT – Import or export of goods
x: Corporation tax is levied on company profits; income tax is on income, customs on imports/exports and VAT on value added.

s: What is the taxable event under GST?
x: GST is levied on supply; excise was on manufacture, VAT on sale and customs on import or export.

s: What was the taxable event for service tax?
x: Service tax was levied on the provision of a service; it is now subsumed in GST.

s: Which of the following pairs of tax and taxable event is correctly matched?
x: Customs is levied on import or export; excise is on manufacture, VAT on sale and GST on supply.

s: Which kind of taxes is generally progressive in nature?
x: Direct taxes are generally progressive, while indirect taxes may be regressive; a higher direct-tax share improves progressivity.

s: A reduction in direct taxes is most likely to produce which immediate effect, other things remaining equal?
o: Lower disposable income and lower consumption demand
Lower disposable income but higher tax buoyancy by definition
Higher disposable income and higher consumption demand
x: A cut in direct taxes raises disposable income, which can increase consumption demand. It may also support savings and investment.

s: Under Article 271 of the Constitution, how are surcharge proceeds treated?
o: They are compulsorily shared with States through the divisible pool
They are collected only by States
They are transferred exclusively to local bodies
They are retained by the Centre and are not shared with States
x: Surcharges under Article 271 are retained by the Centre and are not shared with States. Cesses are also outside the divisible pool.

s: Which of the following is NOT levied by States or local bodies?
x: Customs duty is a Union levy; profession, entertainment, road and property taxes are levied by States or local bodies.

s:
Consider the following statements about the tax on professions, trades and employments:
1. It has no constitutional ceiling.
2. It is a State levy under Article 276.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Profession tax is a State levy under Article 276, with a ceiling of ₹2,500 per year.

s: From which date did the 80th Constitutional Amendment, 2000, on sharing Union taxes with States, take effect?
x: The 80th Amendment was made in 2000 but took effect from 1 April 1996.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law?
x: Article 265 establishes the constitutional requirement that every levy and collection of tax must have the authority of law.

s: Agricultural income tax can constitutionally be levied only by the States under which entry?
x: Agricultural income tax is assigned to the States under Entry 46 of the State List.

s: How many taxing entries does the State List contain?
x: The Union List has 15 taxing entries, the State List 20 and the Concurrent List 3.

s: With whom does the residuary taxing power, under which gift, wealth and expenditure taxes were levied, rest?
x: Residuary taxing power lies with Parliament, the basis of gift, wealth and expenditure taxes.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution can a State levy a tax on professions, trades and employments?
x: Article 276 lets States levy profession tax, with a ceiling of ₹2,500 a year.

s: Under which Section of the Income-tax Act is agricultural income exempt?
x: Agricultural income is exempt under Section 10(1); only States can tax it.

s: Which of the following is treated as agricultural income under income tax?
o: Income from sale of nursery saplings
x: Income from nursery saplings is agricultural income; poultry and dairy income are not.

s: How many taxing entries are there in the Union List of the Constitution?
x: The Union List has 15 taxing entries, the State List 20 and the Concurrent List 3.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the leading components of Andhra Pradesh’s own-tax revenue in 2024–25?
x: In Andhra Pradesh, SGST contributed 38% and State Excise contributed 22% of own-tax revenue in 2024–25.

s: Which is the largest component of the revenue receipts of the States?
x: Own tax revenue is about half of States' revenue receipts (FY25); share in central taxes is second.

s: From which date was GST introduced in India?
x: GST, an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, came into effect on 1 July 2017.

s: Who chaired the Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee that suggested the introduction of VAT in India?
x: The Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee headed by L.K. Jha in 1976 suggested VAT for India.

s: When was MODVAT introduced in India?
x: MODVAT came on 1 March 1986; CENVAT followed on 1 April 2000, Haryana's VAT on 1 April 2003 and nationwide State VAT on 1 April 2005.

s: Which was the first State to adopt VAT in India?
x: Haryana adopted VAT on 1 April 2003; State VAT became nationwide on 1 April 2005.

s: To what level did Budget 2015-16 raise the service tax rate from 12%?
x: Service tax rose from 10% to 12% in 2006-07 and from 12% to 14% in Budget 2015-16.

s: In which year was service tax introduced in India on the advice of the Chelliah Committee?
x: Service tax came in 1994-95 on Chelliah's advice.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Value Added Tax (VAT)?
o: It taxes value added at all stages between production and final sale
It is self-enforcing through the invoice-credit trail
x: VAT is non-cascading, multi-stage and self-enforcing, and it improves revenue buoyancy rather than reducing it.

s: Why is VAT called a self-enforcing tax?
o: It is collected only by the Centre
Its invoice-credit trail makes each buyer check the seller's tax
It is levied only at the final stage of sale
Its rates are fixed by the Finance Commission
x: A buyer gets credit only for tax shown on the seller's invoice, so each stage checks the earlier one.

s: From which date was CENVAT, which replaced MODVAT in Union excise, introduced?
x: CENVAT replaced MODVAT on 1 April 2000.

s: From which date was State VAT introduced across the country?
x: Haryana adopted VAT first in 2003; State VAT went nationwide on 1 April 2005.

s: From 2012-13, service tax at 12% applied to all services except those in which list?
x: From 2012-13 service tax applied to all services except those in the negative list.

s: Which tax was the single largest source of tax revenue in the Budget Estimate for 2026–27?
x: Income tax was identified as the single largest tax source in the 2026–27 Budget Estimate.

s: Which taxes dominated India's tax revenue during the early planning decades?
o: Direct taxes such as income and corporation tax
Indirect taxes such as excise, customs and sales tax
x: Excise, customs and sales taxes (indirect taxes) dominated in the early planning decades; direct taxes dominate now.

s: What is the share of direct taxes in gross tax revenue in the 2026-27 Budget Estimate?
x: Direct taxes are 61.2% of gross tax revenue in 2026-27 BE, against 38.8% for indirect taxes.

s: In the 2026-27 BE, direct taxes are about what percentage of GDP?
x: Direct taxes are 6.9% of GDP and indirect taxes 4.3% in 2026-27 BE.

s: According to the Budget 2026–27 presentation of the Centre’s rupee, which is the largest single source of the Centre’s receipts?
x: Borrowings and other liabilities constitute 24% of the Centre’s rupee and are the largest overall source. Income tax is the largest individual tax source at 21%.

s: What is the share of corporation tax in the Centre's rupee receipts in the Budget Estimates 2026-27?
x: Corporation tax gives 18 paise of each rupee; income tax gives 21 and borrowings 24.

s:
Arrange the following taxes in descending order of their estimated revenue in the Budget Estimates 2026-27:
1. GST
2. Income tax
3. Corporation tax
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Income tax (₹14.66 lakh crore) is ahead of corporation tax (₹12.31 lakh crore) and GST (₹10.19 lakh crore).

s: What does the Laffer curve indicate?
o: Inflation always falls when unemployment rises
Any increase in tax rates always increases tax revenue
Beyond a certain point, higher tax rates may reduce tax revenue
Income inequality always rises with per capita income
x: The Laffer curve shows that tax revenue may decline when tax rates are increased beyond a certain point.

s: What is a tax whose rate rises with income at first and then becomes flat called?
x: A degressive tax rate rises initially and then levels off; a proportional tax has one rate for all.

s: Under a progressive tax, what happens to the average tax burden as income rises?
o: First rises and then becomes flat
x: Higher income slabs are taxed at higher marginal rates, so the average tax burden increases with income.

s: What is a tax charged at one rate for all income levels called?
x: A proportional tax has one rate for all; a flat-rate sales tax is an example.

s: What kind of tax system does India have?
o: Progressive in nature but overall degressive
x: Progressive direct taxes combine with regressive indirect taxes, making the system progressive in nature but overall degressive.

s: What does the Chelliah approach to tax reform mainly favour?
o: Abolition of all tax exemptions without widening the base
Higher tax rates with a narrow base
Lower tax rates with a broader tax base
x: The Chelliah approach favours base widening through more taxpayers and fewer exemptions, together with lower rates rather than rate hikes.

s: What is the shape of the Laffer curve, with zero tax revenue at both a 0% and a 100% tax rate?
x: Revenue is zero at the two extreme rates and positive in between, so the Laffer curve is an inverted U.

s: The Laffer curve is associated with which economist (1974)?
x: Arthur Laffer drew the curve in 1974; the term was coined by Jude Wanniski.

s: Who coined the term 'Laffer curve'?
x: The curve is Arthur Laffer's idea (1974), but the term was coined by Jude Wanniski.

s:
Assertion (A): A simpler tax system raises productivity in the economy.
Reason (R): A simpler tax system removes deadweight costs and distortions in the allocation of resources.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Simplification removes deadweight costs and allocation distortions, and that is why productivity rises; R explains A.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Parthasarathi Shome?
o: The Shome Committee (2012) dealt with GAAR
He recommended VAT at the manufacturing stage, leading to MODVAT
The Shome Committee advised scrapping retrospective tax
The Tax Administration Reform Commission (2013) was headed by him
x: VAT at the manufacturing stage (MODVAT) came from the L.K. Jha Committee (1976), not Shome.

s: In which year was the Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee that proposed VAT in India set up?
x: The L.K. Jha Committee (1976) proposed VAT at the manufacturing stage, leading to MODVAT.

s: What did the Parthasarathi Shome committee of 2012 deal with?
x: Shome (2012) reviewed GAAR and recommended dropping retrospective tax; the 2013 TARC on administration was also under him.

s: Who headed the Task Forces of 2002 that gave reports on both direct and indirect taxes?
x: The Vijay Kelkar Task Forces (2002) gave two reports, one on direct and one on indirect taxes.

s: What is a payment made for a specific service, involving quid pro quo, called?
x: A fee is paid for a specific service and involves quid pro quo; a tax has no direct quid pro quo.

s: What is an additional charge levied on the tax payable called?
x: A surcharge is an additional charge on tax payable, so none is due when no tax is due; a cess is imposed for a specific purpose.

s: What is a levy described as a 'tax on tax' for a specific purpose, ending once the purpose is met, called?
x: A cess is levied for a specific purpose and ends when the purpose is met; it is not shared with States.

s: What was the Clean Energy Cess on coal (2010) renamed in Budget 2016-17?
x: The Clean Energy Cess on coal, from the Finance Act 2010, was renamed Clean Environment Cess in Budget 2016-17.

s: Which tax is levied as a fixed amount per unit of weight or quantity of a commodity?
x: A specific tax is a fixed amount per unit; an ad valorem tax is a percentage of value.

s: How is an ad valorem tax levied on a commodity?
o: As a fixed amount per unit of quantity
As an extra charge on the tax payable
As a percentage of the value of the commodity
As a payment for a specific service
x: Ad valorem means 'according to value': the tax is a percentage of the commodity's value.

s: The tax-GDP ratio is total tax revenue divided by which of the following?
x: The tax-GDP ratio uses nominal GDP; a low ratio may reflect a large informal sector or high evasion.

s: What tax-GDP ratio does the World Bank regard as a tipping point for sustainable growth?
x: The World Bank benchmark is 15 per cent; India's 2001-2022 average was 16.36 per cent.

s: What does a falling tax-GDP ratio imply, other things remaining unchanged?
o: Tax revenue is growing slower than GDP, weakening fiscal space and increasing borrowing requirements
Tax revenue is growing faster than GDP and fiscal space is expanding
Tax buoyancy is necessarily above one
x: A falling ratio indicates that tax revenue is growing more slowly than GDP. This weakens fiscal space and may lead to greater borrowing.

s: What was India's average tax-GDP ratio for 2001-22?
x: India averaged 16.36% in 2001-22, the lowest among emerging economies and below the OECD.

s: What is the combined (Centre and States) tax-GDP ratio of India?
x: The combined ratio is about 19.6%; the Centre's is about 11.5% post-pandemic and States' own tax about 7% of GSDP.

s:
Consider the following statements about the tax-GDP ratio:
1. A low ratio points to a large informal sector or high tax evasion.
2. A falling ratio means revenue is growing slower than GDP.
3. The World Bank regards 25% as the tipping point.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: A low ratio reflects informality or evasion and a falling ratio means buoyancy below 1; the World Bank tipping point is 15%, not 25%.

s: What was the Centre's gross tax revenue as a percentage of GDP in 2019-20, as per the Economic Survey 2021-22?
x: The Centre's gross tax revenue was 9.9% of GDP in 2019-20; it rose to about 11.5% after the pandemic.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was the Centre's gross tax revenue as a share of GDP after the pandemic (FY22-FY25)?
x: The Centre's gross tax-GDP ratio was about 11.5% in FY22-FY25, up from 9.9% in 2019-20.

s: How does India's average tax-GDP ratio of 16.36% (2001-22) compare with other economies?
o: Lowest among emerging economies and below the OECD
x: India's average tax-GDP ratio is the lowest among emerging economies and below the OECD level.

s: What is the response of tax revenue to GDP, excluding discretionary changes in rates and base, called?
x: Tax elasticity excludes discretionary changes, while tax buoyancy includes them.

s: Tax buoyancy, unlike tax elasticity, includes the effect of which of the following?
o: Discretionary changes in tax rates and base
x: Buoyancy includes discretionary changes in rates and base; elasticity excludes them.

s: What is the buoyancy of direct taxes in the 2026-27 BE?
x: Direct tax buoyancy is 1.1 against 0.3 for indirect taxes and 0.8 gross.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, to what level did buoyant revenues help bring down the fiscal deficit in FY26?
x: Buoyant revenues helped the fiscal deficit fall to 4.4% of GDP in FY26.

s: What is the buoyancy of indirect taxes in the 2026-27 Budget Estimates?
x: Indirect-tax buoyancy is only 0.3 (GST not keeping pace), against 1.1 for direct taxes and 0.8 overall.

s: Which body's 2004 work related to implementation of the FRBM framework and proposed a GST roadmap?
x: The Kelkar Task Force covered direct and indirect taxes in 2002 and FRBM implementation with a GST roadmap in 2004.

s: On whose recommendations was the 1992 revision of wealth tax based?
x: The Raja Chelliah Committee advocated lower rates, a broader base and fewer exemptions and formed the basis of the 1992 wealth-tax revision.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Nicholas Kaldor – Expenditure, wealth and gift taxes
Wanchoo Committee – Black money and tax evasion
Raja J. Chelliah Committee – Taxation of agricultural wealth and income
K.N. Raj – Taxation of agricultural wealth and income
x: The Raja Chelliah Committee focused on lower rates and a broader tax base; agricultural wealth and income was K.N. Raj's focus.

s: What did the Wanchoo Committee (1971) mainly deal with?
x: The Wanchoo (Direct Taxes Enquiry) Committee of 1971 dealt with black money and evasion.

s: Which of the following pairs of committee and focus is correctly matched?
o: Justice R.V. Easwar – Simplifying the Income-tax Act
x: Easwar (2015-16) worked on simplifying the Income-tax Act; Rustagi on CBDT restructuring, Akhilesh Ranjan on the DTC and Wanchoo on black money.

s: Nicholas Kaldor's 1956 report recommended which taxes?
o: Expenditure, wealth, gift and capital gains taxes
x: Kaldor (1956) recommended expenditure, wealth, gift and capital gains taxes.

s: What did the T.R. Rustagi Committee deal with?
x: The T.R. Rustagi Committee dealt with restructuring of the CBDT.

s: Who headed the task force whose 2019 report dealt with the Direct Taxes Code?
x: The Akhilesh Ranjan task force reported on the Direct Taxes Code in 2019.

s: Income tax is generally classified as which of the following?
x: Income tax is a direct tax and is classically progressive because the rate generally rises with taxable income.

s: India's first income tax of 1860 was introduced by James Wilson. Which post did he hold?
o: First Finance Minister of independent India
x: James Wilson, the first Finance Member, introduced income tax in 1860 (Act assent 24 July 1860).

s: To what rates did the 1997-98 'dream budget' cut income tax?
x: FM P. Chidambaram's 1997-98 budget cut rates to 10, 20 and 30% from 15, 30 and 40%.

s: What was the 'one-by-six' scheme in income tax?
o: Compulsory return filing by persons showing any one of six signs of lifestyle
A tax rate of one-sixth of income
A rebate for six kinds of savings
Payment of advance tax in six instalments
x: Under the one-by-six scheme a person meeting any one of six lifestyle criteria had to file a return; telephone was dropped in Budget 2002-03.

s: Which Finance Minister presented the 1997-98 'dream budget' that cut almost every tax?
x: P. Chidambaram's 1997-98 budget cut income-tax rates to 10, 20 and 30%.

s: Under the new tax regime from Budget 2025-26, at what rates are income in the ₹20–24 lakh slab and income above ₹24 lakh taxed respectively?
x: The ₹20–24 lakh slab carries a 25% rate, while income above ₹24 lakh is taxed at 30%.

s: Under the first new optional income-tax regime of Budget 2020-21, at what rate was income in the Rs 5 lakh to Rs 7.5 lakh slab taxed?
x: In the 2020-21 new regime, 0-2.5 lakh was nil, 2.5-5 lakh 5%, 5-7.5 lakh 10% (APPSC 2019 key), 7.5-10 lakh 15% and 10-12.5 lakh 20%. So 5%, 15% and 20% belong to other slabs.

s: Under which Section is India's default, exemption-free new income-tax regime provided?
x: Section 115BAC provides the default exemption-free new regime; the old regime with deductions remains optional.

s: Budget 2023-24 cut the highest surcharge under the new regime, for income above ₹2 crore, from 37% to what level?
x: Budget 2023-24 reduced the highest surcharge from 37% to 25% for income above ₹2 crore under the new regime.

s: Under the new tax regime, up to what income does a salaried individual pay no income tax?
x: The ₹12 lakh Section 87A rebate limit plus the ₹75,000 standard deduction gives the ₹12.75 lakh threshold for salaried individuals.

s: Under the new tax regime slabs from Budget 2025-26, at what rate is income of ₹4-8 lakh taxed?
x: Income up to ₹4 lakh is nil and ₹4-8 lakh is taxed at 5%.

s: What is the standard deduction available to salaried taxpayers under the new regime?
x: A ₹75,000 standard deduction takes the salaried tax-free limit from ₹12 lakh to ₹12.75 lakh.

s: What change did Budget 2026-27 make to the new-regime income-tax slabs?
o: Raised the rebate limit to ₹15 lakh
x: The Budget 2025-26 slabs remain unchanged in 2026-27.

s: Under which Section of the Income-tax Act is the rebate given that makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free under the new regime?
x: The Section 87A rebate makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free; 115BAC is the new regime itself.

s: When did the Income-tax Act, 1961 come into effect?
x: The 1961 Act took effect from 1 April 1962.

s: Under FAST-DS 2026, what effective burden does a 30% tax plus an equal additional amount give?
x: 30% tax plus an equal additional amount makes 60%; the threshold is ₹1 crore, or ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets.

s: Vivad se Vishwas primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Introduction of a global minimum corporate tax
x: Vivad se Vishwas is a direct-tax dispute resolution scheme under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020; a second scheme was introduced in 2024.

s: What total levy did the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (2016), introduced after demonetisation, carry?
x: PMGKY 2016 carried a 50% levy; the 1997 scheme was VDIS, not PMGKY.

s: What total levy did the Income Declaration Scheme 2016 carry?
x: IDS 2016 carried 45%; PMGKY 50% and FAST-DS 60%.

s: In which year was the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act passed?
x: The Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act was passed in 2020; a second scheme came in 2024.

s: Under FAST-DS 2026, what is the general disclosure limit for foreign assets of small taxpayers?
x: The limit is ₹1 crore, or ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets.

s:
Consider the following statements about black money disclosure schemes:
1. The Income Declaration Scheme ran from 1 June to 30 September 2016.
2. PMGKY 2016 carried a lower levy than IDS 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IDS ran from 1 June to 30 September 2016 at 45%; PMGKY carried a higher 50% levy.

s: In which year was the Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme (VDIS) launched?
x: VDIS 1997 allowed voluntary disclosure of black income; IDS and PMGKY followed in 2016.

s: Under FAST-DS 2026, declarants get immunity under which Act?
x: FAST-DS 2026 gives immunity under the Black Money Act, 2015.

s: Under FAST-DS 2026, up to what value can previously taxed but unreported foreign assets be disclosed on paying a ₹1 lakh fee?
x: The limit is ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets; the general limit is ₹1 crore.

s: Minimum Alternate Tax is primarily imposed on companies which:
o: Have no book profits but earn only agricultural income
Are registered as unlisted start-ups receiving share premium
Show book profits but otherwise pay little or no regular income tax
x: MAT taxes so-called zero-tax companies on their book profits, ensuring a minimum tax liability despite low or nil regular income-tax liability.

s: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 cut the tax rate for domestic companies from 30% to what level?
x: The 2019 Act cut the rate to 22% and set 15% for new manufacturing companies; MAT does not apply to those opting in.

s: Under Section 115BAB, what base tax rate do new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019 pay?
x: Section 115BAB gives a 15% rate (effective about 17.01%); Section 115BAA gives 22% (effective about 25.17%).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MAT under Budget 2026-27?
o: It was made a final tax
New MAT credit continues to be allowed after 1 April 2026
Before the change, MAT was 15% of book profits
x: Budget 2026-27 cut MAT from 15% to 14% and made it a final tax; no new MAT credit is allowed after 1 April 2026.

s: What is the approximate effective tax rate for existing domestic companies under Section 115BAA?
x: Section 115BAA has a 22% base rate and an effective rate of about 25.17%.

s: What is the approximate effective tax rate for new manufacturing companies under Section 115BAB?
x: Section 115BAB has a 15% base rate and an effective rate of about 17.01%.

s: After being withdrawn in 1990, in which Budget was MAT restarted?
x: MAT came in Budget 1987-88, was withdrawn in 1990 and restarted in Budget 1996-97.

s: In which Budget was the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) first introduced under Section 115J?
x: MAT came in Budget 1987-88 (Section 115J), was withdrawn in 1990 and restarted in Budget 1996-97.

s: In which year was securities transaction tax (STT) introduced in India?
x: STT came in 2004; estate duty was 1953, wealth tax 1957 and gift tax 1958.

s: Which Finance Minister introduced expenditure tax in 1958 on Nicholas Kaldor's advice?
x: Finance Minister T.T. Krishnamachari introduced the expenditure tax in 1958 on Kaldor's advice.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT)?
o: It was abolished with effect from 1 April 2020
Dividends are now taxed only in the hands of the company paying them
Dividends are now taxed in the hands of shareholders
x: After DDT was abolished from 1 April 2020 by Budget 2020-21, dividends became taxable in the shareholders' hands, not the company's.

s: As a general rule, a capital asset held for up to how many months is a short-term capital asset?
x: Generally, an asset held up to 24 months is short-term; rural agricultural land is not a capital asset at all.

s: Indexation for computing capital gains uses which of the following?
o: Wholesale Price Index notified by the RBI, with base year 1991-92
Cost Inflation Index notified by CBDT, with base year 2001-02
Consumer Price Index notified by SEBI, with base year 2011-12
GDP deflator notified by the Finance Commission, with base year 2004-05
x: Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by the CBDT, and the stated base year is 2001-02.

s: 'Angel tax', often called a tax on venture capital, refers to tax on which of the following?
o: Share premium received by unlisted start-ups in excess of fair value
Capital gains on sale of rural agricultural land
Interest earned by foreign investors on government securities
x: Angel tax was a tax on the share premium received by unlisted start-ups above fair value (APPSC 2019). It came in 2012 and was abolished in Budget 2024-25.

s: In which Budget was angel tax, levied from 2012 on share premium of unlisted start-ups, abolished?
x: Angel tax was abolished in Budget 2024-25.

s:
Consider the following statements about special direct taxes:
1. Estate duty was introduced in 1953 and abolished in 1985.
2. Wealth tax was introduced in 1957 and abolished in 2015.
3. Gift tax is still in force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Estate duty ran 1953-1985 and wealth tax 1957-2015; gift tax was abolished in October 1998.

s: When was gift tax, introduced in April 1958, abolished?
x: Gift tax was abolished in October 1998.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about capital gains?
o: Capital gains arise on transfer of a capital asset
Rural agricultural land is a capital asset
Tax on sale of inherited property is capital gains tax
Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index
x: Rural agricultural land is not a capital asset; the other statements are correct.

s: What is the rate of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax in India as of August 2026?
x: LTCG is taxed at 12.5%; an asset held up to 24 months is generally short-term.

s: With which of the following is the OECD/G20 project on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) associated?
o: 15 actions to address base erosion and profit shifting
x: BEPS is an OECD/G20 project comprising 15 actions aimed at combating base erosion and profit shifting.

s:
Consider the following statements about OECD Pillar Two:
1. It applies to all companies regardless of size.
2. It provides for a 15% global minimum corporate tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pillar Two sets a 15% global minimum corporate tax for large multinational enterprises, not all companies.

s: The Vodafone tax dispute led to which of the following developments?
o: A 50% levy under PMGKY after demonetisation
A retrospective amendment in 2012 relating to indirect transfers, followed by withdrawal of retrospective demands in 2021
A 2016 levy on online advertising followed by its abolition in 2025
A 15% global minimum corporate tax under OECD Pillar Two
x: Following the Supreme Court's 2012 Vodafone ruling, indirect transfers were taxed retrospectively through the Finance Act, 2012. The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 withdrew the retrospective demands involving Vodafone and Cairn.

s: Which Act withdrew retrospective tax demands in cases such as Vodafone and Cairn?
x: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 withdrew retrospective demands; the Finance Act 2012 had imposed them.

s: To what did the equalisation levy of 6% introduced in 2016 apply?
x: The 6% levy (2016) was on online ads and was abolished from 1 April 2025; the 2% levy (2020) was on e-commerce.

s: At what rate was the equalisation levy on e-commerce supplies imposed in 2020?
x: The 2020 equalisation levy on e-commerce was 2% (dropped in 2024); the 2016 levy on online ads was 6%.

s: From which date was the 6% equalisation levy on online advertisements abolished?
x: The 6% levy on online ads, started in 2016, was abolished from 1 April 2025.

s: In a PAN, which character shows the holder type ('P' for individual, 'C' for company)?
x: PAN is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier whose 4th character shows the holder type.

s: With what is Project Insight, launched in 2017 and made operational in 2019, associated?
o: Artificial intelligence and data analytics for tax compliance
Issuance of corporate bonds by SEBI
Digitisation of land records for State Governments
x: Project Insight uses artificial intelligence and data analytics to improve tax compliance.

s: When were faceless assessment and the Taxpayers' Charter launched?
x: They were launched on 13 August 2020 under 'Transparent Taxation - Honouring the Honest'; faceless appeals followed in September 2020.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)?
o: It is the apex body for direct taxes
It is a statutory body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963
It is the cadre controller of the Indian Revenue Service
It is placed in the Department of Expenditure
x: CBDT is placed in the Department of Revenue, not the Department of Expenditure.

s: Under which Act is the CBDT a statutory body?
x: CBDT is statutory under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963, and sits in the Department of Revenue.

s: When were faceless appeals in income tax launched?
x: Faceless assessment came on 13 August 2020 and faceless appeals in September 2020.

s: Budget 2026-27 cut TCS on LRS remittances for education and medical purposes from 5% to what level?
x: TCS on LRS for education and medical was cut from 5% to 2% in 2026-27.

s: What is 'e-Sahyog' of the Income Tax Department?
o: An online check of mismatches in returns for compliance
A disclosure scheme for foreign assets
x: e-Sahyog lets taxpayers settle mismatches online without a physical visit.

s: What does the Annual Information Statement (AIS) of the Income Tax Department show?
o: Only the PAN details of a taxpayer
All reported financial transactions of a taxpayer
x: AIS shows all reported transactions of a taxpayer and is used to pre-fill returns (2021).

s: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which one of the following replaces the concepts of the Assessment Year and the Previous Year?
x: The Act introduces a single 12-month ‘Tax Year’ beginning on 1 April, replacing the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year terminology.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961.
2. The replacement took effect from 1 April 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act with effect from 1 April 2026, not 2025.

s: From which date did the Income-tax Act, 2025 come into force?
x: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act with effect from 1 April 2026, not 2025.

s: Who headed the committee that worked out the Revenue Neutral Rate for GST?
x: The Arvind Subramanian committee (2015) worked out the RNR, the rate that keeps revenue equal to the pre-GST level.

s: Which State was the first to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment?
x: Assam was the first State to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment, which required ratification by the States.

s: When did the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act receive Presidential assent?
x: Presidential assent came on 8 September 2016; GST rolled out on 1 July 2017.

s: Which of the following pairs of GST body and chair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers – Arvind Subramanian
Revenue Neutral Rate Committee – Arvind Subramanian
Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers – Asim Dasgupta
x: The Empowered Committee was chaired by Asim Dasgupta; Arvind Subramanian chaired the Revenue Neutral Rate Committee.

s: India's GST, recommended by the Vijay Kelkar Task Force, follows the dual model of which country?
x: India's GST follows the Canadian dual model; France is where the GST concept was first used.

s: Which Act did the Constitution (122nd Amendment) Bill, 2014 become?
x: The 122nd Amendment Bill became the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016. The Bill number and the enacted Amendment Act number are different.

s: GST was implemented in India on which date?
x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, after the 101st Constitutional Amendment of 2016.

s: What Revenue Neutral Rate did the Revenue Neutral Rate Committee recommend?
x: The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee, chaired by Arvind Subramanian, recommended an RNR of about 15–15.5% and a standard rate of 17–18%.

s: Which was the last State to adopt GST?
x: Jammu and Kashmir adopted GST last, on 8 July 2017; Assam was the first to ratify the amendment.

s: The GST concept was first used in which country?
x: GST was first used in France; India follows the Canadian dual model.

s: Who was the first chair of the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers on GST?
x: Asim Dasgupta first chaired the Empowered Committee, which gave 'A Model and Roadmap for GST' in 2008.

s: When was the GST Council constituted by the President?
x: The GST Council was formed by the President in September 2016, after the 101st Amendment Act.

s: Which Constitution Amendment Bill on GST, introduced in March 2011, lapsed?
x: The 115th Amendment Bill (2011) lapsed; the 122nd Bill (2014) became the 101st Amendment Act, 2016.

s:
Arrange the following events relating to GST in chronological order:
1. 101st Amendment Act gets Presidential assent
2. 122nd Amendment Bill is tabled
3. GST is rolled out across India
4. GST 2.0 comes into effect
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The 122nd Bill came in December 2014, assent to the 101st Act in September 2016, rollout on 1 July 2017 and GST 2.0 in September 2025.

s: Under which government was GST first proposed in India?
x: GST was first proposed under the Vajpayee government.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GST was first proposed in India under the Vajpayee government.
2. The GST concept was first used in Canada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: GST was first proposed under Vajpayee; the concept was first used in France, while India follows Canada's dual model.

s: Who was the brand ambassador of GST in India?
x: Amitabh Bachchan was the GST brand ambassador.

s: In which year was the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers set up?
x: The Empowered Committee was set up in 2000, first chaired by Asim Dasgupta.

s: In which year did the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers release 'A Model and Roadmap for GST'?
x: It released 'A Model and Roadmap for GST' in April 2008.

s: When did the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers release its First Discussion Paper on GST?
x: The First Discussion Paper came in November 2009.

s:
Consider the following statements about GST:
1. Its taxable event is manufacture.
2. It is a multi-stage, destination-based consumption tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: GST is a multi-stage, destination-based tax on value addition whose taxable event is supply, not manufacture.

s: Why is Goods and Services Tax regarded as the biggest indirect tax reform in India since Independence?
o: replaced the need for all direct taxes
abolished the divisible pool of taxes
created a unified framework for a large number of indirect taxes
transferred all taxation powers to the States
x: GST is considered the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence because it established a unified framework for indirect taxation by subsuming several indirect taxes.

s: What is 'tax on tax', which GST aims to end, known as?
x: Reducing cascading (tax on tax) and creating a unified national market are major GST objectives.

s: Under destination-based GST, revenue ultimately accrues to the jurisdiction where goods or services are:
x: GST is destination-based, so revenue goes to the State where goods or services are consumed, not where they are produced.

s: In which slogan is the objective of GST commonly summed up?
x: GST replaced a fragmented indirect-tax structure with one tax – 'one nation, one tax'.

s: Who was the first chairperson of the GST Council?
x: The Union Finance Minister chairs the Council; Arun Jaitley was its first chair.

s: What is the quorum of the GST Council?
x: The GST Council's quorum is one-half of its total members.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022)?
o: It held GST Council recommendations to be persuasive, not binding
It held that the GST Council is a statutory body
It recognised simultaneous power of Parliament and States to legislate on GST
It described India as a 'flexible federation'
x: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A and was never statutory.

s: Which of the following pairs about voting in the GST Council is correctly matched?
o: All States together – one-half of votes cast
Centre's vote – one-third of votes cast
Centre's vote – one-fourth of votes cast
x: Under Article 279A the Centre has one-third and the States together two-thirds of votes cast; decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority.

s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is chaired by the Union Minister of State for Finance.
2. It is a constitutional body under Article 279A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A chaired by the Union Finance Minister; the MoS is only a member.

s: What is the position of the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance in the GST Council?
x: The Union Finance Minister chairs the Council; the MoS in charge of Revenue or Finance is only a member.

s: Who chooses the Vice-Chairperson of the GST Council?
o: The State members from among themselves
x: The State members of the GST Council choose the Vice-Chairperson from among themselves.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the GST Council?
o: It recommends tax rates, exemptions and threshold limits
It sets up a mechanism to settle Centre-State disputes
Its recommendations bind Parliament and the States
Its proceedings are not invalid because of a vacancy
x: In Mohit Minerals (2022) the Council's recommendations were held persuasive, not binding; legislative power stays with Parliament and the States.

s: What is the ceiling for CGST under the GST Acts?
x: The CGST Act provides a ceiling of 20%. The corresponding IGST ceiling is 40%.

s: How are GST rates normally changed?
o: An order of the Reserve Bank of India
Amending the GST Acts through Parliament in every case
Government notification issued on the recommendation of the GST Council, subject to statutory ceilings
A resolution of the Finance Commission
x: Rates are normally changed through government notification on the recommendation of the GST Council, rather than by amending the Acts each time.

s: At the 56th meeting of the GST Council, the tax slabs were identified as which of the following?
o: 5% merit, 18% standard and 40% de-merit or sin
x: The 56th meeting provided for slabs of 5% for merit goods, 18% as the standard rate and 40% for de-merit or sin goods.

s: What is the ceiling rate for IGST under the GST Acts?
x: The GST Acts set ceilings of 20% for CGST and 40% for IGST.

s: To which goods does the 40% rate apply under GST 2.0?
x: GST 2.0 has 5% for merit goods, 18% standard, and 40% for sin and ultra-luxury (de-merit) goods.

s: From which date did the GST 2.0 rate rationalisation come into effect?
x: The 56th Council meeting (3-4 September 2025) approved GST 2.0, effective 22 September 2025.

s: Which State levy was NOT subsumed in GST?
x: Stamp duty is retained outside GST; purchase, luxury and entry taxes were subsumed.

s: Which of the following statements regarding taxes subsumed under GST is incorrect?
o: Central Excise Duty was subsumed under GST.
State VAT was subsumed under GST.
Various other Central and State direct taxes were subsumed under GST.
Service Tax was subsumed under GST.
x: Option C is incorrect: GST replaced indirect taxes such as excise, service tax and State VAT, not direct taxes.

s: Which of the following was subsumed in GST?
x: Entry tax was subsumed in GST; stamp duty, Basic Customs Duty and electricity duty were not.

s:
Consider the following statements about taxes and GST:
1. Service tax and CVD on imports were subsumed in GST.
2. State excise on alcoholic liquor was subsumed in GST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Service tax and CVD were subsumed; State excise on alcoholic liquor was retained outside GST.

s: How many Central and State taxes respectively are conventionally stated to have been subsumed into GST?
x: The conventional classification identifies eight Central taxes and nine State taxes as subsumed into GST.

s: Which of the following is outside the current GST levy?
x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is outside GST, as are electricity, stamp-duty real estate transactions and ATF.

s: Which one of the following is constitutionally excluded from GST rather than merely awaiting a notified date for levy?
x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from GST. The listed petroleum products are constitutionally within GST but have not been brought under it for levy.

s: Which of the following is one of the five petroleum products kept outside the current levy of GST?
x: The five are crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel; lubricating oil is not among them.

s:
Consider the following statements about GST:
1. Exports and supplies to SEZs are zero-rated, with full ITC refund.
2. Nil-rated supplies allow input tax credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Zero-rated supplies (exports, SEZ supplies) get full ITC refund; nil-rated supplies do not permit ITC.

s: Under the GST 2.0 changes referred to in the current tax structure, which of the following is exempted?
o: All motor vehicle insurance premiums without exception
Individual life and health insurance premiums
x: GST 2.0 provides exemption for individual life and health insurance premiums. The exemption is not stated as a blanket exemption for every insurance service.

s: Which medicines were fully exempted from GST in June 2026?
x: Rare-disease medicines were fully exempted from GST in June 2026.

s: A supplier pays tax on inputs and sets it off against the tax payable on outward supplies. What is this facility known as?
x: Input Tax Credit allows tax paid on inputs to be set off against output tax. It helps prevent cascading of taxes.

s: From 1 October 2024, which body hears GST anti-profiteering cases?
x: Anti-profiteering functions moved from NAA to CCI in December 2022 and to the GSTAT Principal Bench from 1 October 2024.

s: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism in GST, from whom to whom is the liability to pay tax shifted?
x: Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.

s: What is the turnover limit for goods under the GST composition scheme?
x: The limit is ₹1.5 crore for goods and ₹50 lakh for services, at 1% and 6%, with no ITC.

s: In December 2022, to which body was the work of the National Anti-Profiteering Authority first transferred?
x: NAA's work went to the CCI in December 2022, and only from 1 October 2024 to the GSTAT Principal Bench.

s: Which Section of the CGST Act requires that the benefit of a GST rate cut or input tax credit be passed on to consumers?
x: Section 171 is the anti-profiteering provision; it requires rate-cut and ITC benefits to reach consumers.

s: What are the turnover limit and tax rate for service providers under the GST composition scheme?
x: Service providers with turnover up to ₹50 lakh pay 6%; for goods the limit is ₹1.5 crore at 1%; no ITC is allowed.

s: What does GST allow in the case of an inverted duty structure?
o: Payment of tax by the recipient
x: Under an inverted duty structure (input tax higher than output tax), refunds of accumulated ITC are allowed.

s: What is the main purpose of e-invoicing?
o: Replace all GST returns with paper invoices
Digitally report invoices, curb fake invoices and verify input-tax credit
Set the GST Council’s voting weights
Determine the annual borrowing limit of States
x: E-invoicing digitally reports invoices, helps curb fake invoices and supports verification of input-tax credit.

s: Above what value of goods is an e-way bill required for their movement?
x: An e-way bill is needed for goods above ₹50,000, valid one day per 200 km.

s: How many digits does a GSTIN have?
x: The GSTIN, issued through the GSTN system, is a 15-digit number.

s: An e-way bill is generally valid for one day for every how many kilometres?
x: An e-way bill, needed for goods above ₹50,000, is valid one day per 200 km.

s: In which year was GSTN made a fully government-owned company?
x: GSTN began as a not-for-profit company with 51% private holding and became fully government-owned in 2018.

s: What was the share of private institutions in GSTN before it became fully government-owned?
x: GSTN was set up with Centre 24.5%, States 24.5% and private institutions 51%; it became government-owned in 2018.

s: Under Budget 2026-27, within how many working days is GST registration given automatically to low-risk applicants?
x: Low-risk applicants (liability up to ₹2.5 lakh a month) get automated registration within 3 working days.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with inter-State GST?
x: Article 269A concerns inter-State GST; 246A gives GST law-making power and 279A provides for the GST Council.

s: Under Article 246A, for which kind of supply does Parliament alone have the power to make GST laws?
o: Made by a local authority only
x: Article 246A gives Parliament and State Legislatures concurrent GST legislative power, but Parliament alone legislates in relation to inter-State supplies.

s: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act inserted which Article relating to the GST Council?
x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; the same Amendment omitted Article 268A.

s: By at least how many State Legislatures did the GST constitutional amendment need to be ratified?
x: Since the amendment affected the federal distribution of powers, ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures was required.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 246A gives GST law-making power; 269A covers IGST and 279A the GST Council, while 268A (service tax) was omitted.

s: What happened to Article 268A, relating to service tax, by the 101st Constitutional Amendment?
x: The 101st Amendment omitted Article 268A on service tax, since service tax was subsumed in GST.

s: Before GST, under which entry of the State List was VAT levied?
x: VAT was a State subject under Entry 54 of the State List.

s: Who constitutes the GST Council?
x: The GST Council is formed by the President under Article 279A of the Constitution.

s: GST was introduced in India with effect from 1 July 2017 through which constitutional framework?
o: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 and Articles 246A, 269A and 279A
The 86th Amendment Act and Articles 243G, 243H and 243I
The 73rd Amendment Act and Articles 280, 281 and 282
The 42nd Amendment Act and Articles 301, 302 and 303
x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, with Articles 246A, 269A and 279A forming its key constitutional basis.

s: What annual revenue growth over the 2015-16 base did GST compensation to States assume?
x: Compensation was for five years at 14% annual growth over 2015-16; it ended in June 2022.

s: After the general withdrawal of GST compensation cess from 22 September 2025, on which item did it continue?
x: The cess was scrapped for all goods except tobacco; its levy was extended to March 2026 to repay compensation loans.

s: On what basis is the Health Security se National Security Cess levied on pan masala units?
x: It is levied on machine production capacity, and its proceeds go to the Consolidated Fund of India without being shared with States.

s: From 1 February 2026, what replaced the compensation-cess arrangement for tobacco?
o: A special State GST on tobacco
