A customs duty collected by the GST Council
A surcharge under the IGST Act
x: Higher excise was imposed on tobacco under the Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025, while pan masala units got the Health Security se National Security Cess.

s: Under the GST Compensation Act, in what ratio is any unutilised balance at the end split between the Centre and the States?
x: The unutilised balance is split 50:50 – half to the Centre and half shared among the States.

s: When did the GST compensation cess finally end?
x: Compensation ended in June 2022, cess was scrapped for all but tobacco on 22 Sep 2025, and it ended on 31 March 2026.

s: For how many years did the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 provide compensation to States?
x: The Act gave 5 years of compensation, assuming 14% annual growth over the 2015-16 base; it ended in June 2022.

s: When did GST compensation to States end?
x: Compensation ended in June 2022; the cess continued to repay loans and ended on 31 March 2026.

s: Where does the money from the Health Security se National Security Cess on pan masala units go?
o: Consolidated Fund of India, not shared with States
x: The cess goes to the Consolidated Fund of India and is not shared with the States.

s: Under which Act was higher excise on tobacco levied from 1 February 2026?
x: Higher tobacco excise came from 1 February 2026 under the Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025.

s: To whom is IGST revenue finally settled?
x: GST is destination-based, so IGST revenue goes to the consuming State.

s: Which is the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue (2024-25 RE)?
x: SGST is AP's largest own tax source at about Rs 36,296 crore (38%); State excise (22%) is second.

s: Which taxes does the Centre administer and collect under GST?
x: The Centre collects CGST and IGST, States collect SGST, and the GST Council recommends.

s: In which territories is UTGST levied on intra-UT supplies?
x: UTGST is levied by the Centre for Union Territories without a legislature.

s: On which supplies does the Centre levy IGST?
x: IGST under Article 269A applies to inter-State supplies and imports, and settles to the consuming State.

s: In which month did India record its highest gross GST collection of ₹2.43 lakh crore?
x: Gross GST hit a record ₹2.43 lakh crore in April 2026.

s: In which month did monthly gross GST collections first exceed ₹2 lakh crore?
x: Monthly gross GST collections crossed ₹2 lakh crore for the first time in April 2024.

s: What was India's gross GST collection in FY 2024-25?
o: ₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.84 lakh crore per month
₹24.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.43 lakh crore per month
₹17.4 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.82 lakh crore per month
x: Gross GST collection in FY 2024-25 was ₹22.08 lakh crore, averaging ₹1.84 lakh crore per month.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GST collections in April 2026?
o: Gross collection reached a record ₹2.43 lakh crore
It was the first month gross collection crossed ₹2 lakh crore
x: Gross GST first crossed ₹2 lakh crore in April 2024; April 2026 set the record of ₹2.43 lakh crore (+8.7%) with net ₹2.11 lakh crore.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, a cut in GST rates may have what effect on revenue?
o: Volume effects may offset the initial revenue loss
It necessarily eliminates all future GST revenue
It reduces transaction volumes in every sector
It affects only customs revenue and not GST revenue
x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 observed that increased volume of transactions following a rate cut may offset the associated revenue loss.

s: How did the Economic Survey 2025-26 describe GST 2.0?
x: GST 2.0 was described as the third pillar of tax reform, after the 2019 corporate tax cut and the 2025 personal income-tax reform.

s: In which financial year was the highest-ever annual gross GST collection of ₹22.27 lakh crore recorded?
x: FY 2025-26 recorded the highest-ever ₹22.27 lakh crore (+8.3%); FY 2024-25 was ₹22.08 lakh crore.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, GST 2.0 is the third pillar of tax reform after which two earlier reforms?
o: 2017 GST rollout and 2019 GST Council reform
2019 corporate tax cut and 2025 personal income-tax reform
x: The Survey called GST 2.0 the third pillar after the 2019 corporate tax cut and the 2025 personal income-tax reform.

s: What range of Revenue Neutral Rate (RNR) for GST did the Arvind Subramanian Committee (2015) recommend?
x: The CEA committee (Dec 2015) put the RNR at 15-15.5%, preferring 15%; 17-18% was its standard rate.

s: Who headed the committee that recommended the Revenue Neutral Rate and the structure of GST rates in December 2015?
x: Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian headed the committee; it suggested an RNR of 15-15.5% and a standard rate of 17-18%.

s: Which of the following is the most direct contribution of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to inter-State commerce?
o: Replacement of input tax credit by a turnover tax
Creation of a common national market through tax harmonisation
Exemption of all inter-State supplies from taxation
Retention of State border check-posts for all goods
x: GST created a common national market by harmonising indirect taxation across States. It also helped reduce the cascading effect through input tax credit.

s: An e-way bill under GST is valid for one day for every how many kilometres?
x: Validity is one day per 200 km; the e-way bill is mandatory above ₹50,000.

s: What was the main result of removing inter-State check-posts after the rollout of e-way bills?
o: A shift from digital to manual tax reporting
Reduced transit time and logistics costs
The abolition of input tax credit
x: The replacement of physical checks and the dismantling of border check-posts reduced truck waiting time, transit time and logistics costs.

s: How did the GST taxpayer base change between 2017 and 2025?
o: The taxpayer base remained unchanged at 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 66.5 lakh to 1.51 crore
The taxpayer base declined from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
x: The taxpayer base expanded from 66.5 lakh in 2017 to 1.51 crore in 2025, indicating greater formalisation.

s: What flat rate of tax does a taxpayer under the GST composition scheme pay on goods?
x: The composition scheme levies 1% on goods and 6% on services, and the taxpayer cannot claim ITC.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GST compliance for small businesses?
o: The composition scheme has eased the compliance burden
Automated registration has eased the compliance burden
Multiple returns and ITC matching remain a burden
The reform agenda proposes replacing pre-filled returns with manual filing
x: The reform agenda calls for pre-filled returns, time-bound digital registration and automated exporter refunds, not manual filing.

s: Above what value of goods in transit is an e-way bill required under GST?
x: An e-way bill is needed for movement of goods worth more than ₹50,000; it is valid one day per 200 km.

s: Up to what annual turnover can a supplier of goods opt for the GST composition scheme?
x: Goods suppliers with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (₹50 lakh for services) can opt for the composition scheme.

s:
Consider the following statements about the GST composition scheme:
1. A goods dealer pays a flat 1% tax.
2. A composition dealer can claim input tax credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Composition dealers in goods pay a flat 1%, but they get no input tax credit, so only statement 1 is correct.

s: Under the GST composition scheme, at what flat rate do service providers pay tax?
x: Composition dealers pay 1% on goods and 6% on services, with no input tax credit.

s: Which of the following is done by bogus entities in input tax credit (ITC) fraud?
o: Paying output tax twice on genuine transactions
Issuing invoices without actual supply of goods or services
Using only government invoices for exports
Claiming refunds on petroleum products outside GST
x: Bogus entities issue invoices without any corresponding supply in order to fraudulently claim input tax credit.

s: Which States does the destination principle of GST generally favour?
o: States with the highest rates of State excise duty
Producing States because tax is collected at the point of manufacture
Consuming States because taxation follows the place of consumption
x: GST follows the destination principle, under which consuming States benefit because revenue is associated with the place of consumption.

s: Why does input tax credit pile up and block working capital under an Inverted Duty Structure?
o: Tax on output exceeds tax on inputs
Tax paid on inputs exceeds tax payable on output
IGST is not apportioned to States
x: When the tax on inputs is higher than the tax on output, ITC piles up and blocks the working capital of businesses.

s:
Consider the following statements about an inter-State supply under GST:
1. IGST is levied by the Centre and apportioned.
2. The State share of IGST goes to the producing State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IGST is levied by the Centre and apportioned; the destination (consuming) State receives the State share.

s: Which of the following continue to remain outside the GST framework?
x: Petroleum and electricity remain outside the GST framework.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT)?
o: Its Principal Bench is located in Mumbai
It was created through the Finance Act, 2024
It was formally launched in September 2025
x: GSTAT's Principal Bench is at New Delhi, not Mumbai.

s: As of mid-2025, which problem was associated with the GST Appellate Tribunal?
o: State benches had exclusive jurisdiction over direct taxes
The tribunal had replaced the Supreme Court as the final court of appeal
Only the New Delhi Principal Bench had been abolished
Functional benches were absent in many States despite notification
x: Although GSTAT had been notified, functional benches were absent in many States as of mid-2025, causing appeals to accumulate in High Courts.

s: With reference to Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022), which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: GST Council recommendations – Binding on legislatures
Status of GST Council – Statutory body
Source of simultaneous GST power – Article 279A
x: The Court called India a flexible federation; recommendations are persuasive, the simultaneous power flows from Article 246A, and the Council is constitutional.

s: Why does the Centre have an effective veto in the GST Council?
o: Because the Centre’s one-third vote can prevent a three-fourths majority
Because the Centre has two-thirds of the weighted vote
Because State representatives cannot vote on tax matters
Because the Centre alone nominates all State members
x: Since three-fourths weighted support is required and the Centre holds one-third of the vote, the Centre can block a proposal without its support.

s: Which of the following groups of petroleum products is covered by the GST law but remains outside GST taxation until a date recommended by the GST Council?
o: Crude oil, petrol, diesel, natural gas and ATF
Natural gas, electricity, alcohol, tobacco and ATF
Coal, electricity, iron ore, cement and steel
Gold, silver, diamonds, petrol and coal
x: Crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel are within the GST law but are taxed outside GST until the Council recommends a date under Article 279A(5).

s: Which of the following is a criticism of cesses in the GST framework?
o: They can be imposed only by State legislatures
They are always included in the divisible pool for distribution to States
They remain outside the divisible pool, contributing to concerns over State fiscal autonomy
x: Cesses outside the divisible pool reduce the share available for devolution and are therefore linked with concerns about States’ fiscal autonomy and vertical fiscal imbalance.

s: The GST Appellate Tribunal was launched in September 2025. When did its hearings begin?
x: GSTAT was launched in September 2025 and hearings began in December 2025.

s: In Mohit Minerals (2022), how was the power of Parliament and the States to legislate on GST under Article 246A described?
x: The Court held that Parliament and the States have simultaneous power under Article 246A and the Council's recommendations are only persuasive.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about unresolved GST issues?
o: Petroleum and electricity remain outside GST
The date for taxing petroleum is set on Council recommendation under Article 279A(5)
Cesses lie outside the divisible pool
GST Council recommendations are binding on the States
x: Mohit Minerals held Council recommendations persuasive, not binding; the other three are correct.

s: Where is the Principal Bench of the GST Appellate Tribunal located?
x: GSTAT has its Principal Bench in New Delhi, with State benches.

s: What was the original GST rate structure introduced in 2017, apart from exempt goods and compensation cess?
x: The original GST structure contained slabs of 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, along with exempt goods and compensation cess over 28% for specified goods.

s: What is the GST rate structure from 22 September 2025?
o: 0%, 5% as merit rate, 18% as standard rate and 40% as demerit rate
x: GST 2.0 rationalised the principal slabs into 0%, 5%, 18% and 40%, with 5% as the merit rate, 18% as the standard rate and 40% as the demerit rate.

s: What are the GST rates on rough diamonds and on gold, silver and jewellery, respectively, under the special-rate structure?
x: Rough diamonds attract a special rate of 0.25%, while gold, silver and jewellery attract 3%.

s: What was the four-slab structure of GST originally intended to be?
o: A permanent arrangement for all goods and services
A mechanism for distributing IGST among States
A structure applicable only to petroleum products
x: The four-slab GST structure was conceived as a transitional arrangement rather than a permanent structure.

s: Which of the following pairs about GST 2.0 slab shifts (from 22 September 2025) is correctly matched?
x: About 99% of old 12% items moved to 5%; about 90% of old 28% items moved to 18%, and only the rest to 40%.

s: At which GST Council meeting were the GST 2.0 reforms approved, and from which date did they take effect?
x: The GST 2.0 reforms were approved at the 56th GST Council meeting held on 3–4 September 2025 and became effective on 22 September 2025.

s: Under a multi-rate GST, what does placing near-identical products in different slabs mainly lead to?
x: Differing classification of similar products invites litigation; standardising classification is a pending reform.

s: Under GST 2.0, which of the following falls in the 40% demerit slab?
o: Most items of the old 12% slab
x: Private aircraft, yachts, ultra-luxury cars, tobacco, pan masala and online gaming are at 40%; gold is 3% and rough diamonds 0.25%.

s: Which group of producing States feared revenue loss under the destination-based GST?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
x: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka were identified as manufacturing States that feared losses because GST revenue follows consumption rather than production. This concern contributed to the five-year compensation guarantee.

s: At what assured annual growth rate over the 2015-16 base were States guaranteed GST compensation?
x: Compensation was assured for five years (July 2017 – June 2022) at 14% annual growth over the 2015-16 base.

s: Why was the GST compensation cess continued after the compensation period?
o: Repay loans taken to pay compensation during the COVID-19 period
x: After the compensation period, the cess was continued to repay loans taken for paying GST compensation during the COVID-19 period.

s: From 22 September 2025, the GST compensation cess was scrapped for all goods except which of the following?
x: The compensation cess was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except for tobacco products, on which it continues until cess-account loan obligations are discharged.

s: How is the unused balance of the GST compensation cess to be shared?
o: Entirely to the States in proportion to their population
50% to the Centre and 50% to the States in proportion to their SGST revenue
As per the Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula
x: The unused balance goes 50% to the Centre and 50% to the States, with the States' half shared in proportion to their SGST revenue. It does not all go to the Centre (A), it is not shared by population (B), and the Finance Commission formula (D) does not apply because cess is outside the divisible pool.

s: What has been one major fiscal consequence for States of giving up independent indirect-tax powers under GST?
o: Greater dependence on transfers because of weak own revenues
Automatic equalisation of revenues among all States
Complete elimination of State taxation powers
x: The surrender of independent indirect-tax powers, combined with weak own revenues, has increased States’ dependence on transfers.

s: For which period was GST compensation paid to the States?
x: States got compensation for five years, July 2017 to June 2022, at 14% growth over the 2015-16 base.

s: Which of the following State taxes was subsumed in GST?
x: States gave up VAT, entry tax, luxury tax, entertainment tax and octroi when GST came in.

s: Through which of the following does Andhra Pradesh, a consuming State, mainly benefit from GST?
o: State excise on petroleum under GST
Abolition of its own tax revenue
x: As a consuming State, Andhra Pradesh benefits from the destination principle through IGST settlement.

s: How is 'Net GST' defined for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Gross GST collections minus customs revenue
SGST plus the State’s share of IGST settlement
SGST minus the State’s share of IGST settlement
x: Andhra Pradesh’s Net GST consists of SGST plus its share received through IGST settlement.

s: In May 2026, what did the Andhra Pradesh High Court hold that authorities must do where Central and State GST investigations overlap?
o: Abandon the investigation if the entity operates in more than one State
Decide inter se which authority will proceed
Transfer every case automatically to the Union Government
Both proceed simultaneously against the same entity
x: The Court held that Central and State GST authorities must decide inter se who will proceed against a common entity, thereby preventing dual action.

s: Which is the second-largest contributor to Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue (2024-25 RE)?
x: GST is the largest at about 38% (₹36,296 crore) and State Excise second at about 22% (₹21,300 crore).

s: Which is the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue (2024-25 RE)?
x: GST gives about 38% (₹36,296 crore) of AP's own tax revenue, the largest share; State Excise is second at 22%.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 271 – Surcharge on certain Union taxes for the Union
Article 265 – Taxes without authority of law in emergencies
x: Article 271 provides surcharges wholly for the Union; Article 276 covers professional taxes, Article 293 State borrowing and Article 265 requires authority of law for taxation.

s: Which tax is wholly kept by the Union and not shared with the States?
x: Surcharge under Article 271 is wholly for the Union; corporation tax and customs are in the shared pool.

s: Under Article 268, how are stamp duties levied by the Union dealt with?
o: Collected and kept by the States
Shared as the Finance Commission recommends
Collected by the Union and assigned to States
x: Article 268 duties are levied by the Union but collected and kept by the States.

s:
Consider the following statements about taxes:
1. Corporation tax is a Union tax in the shared pool.
2. Agricultural income tax is a Union tax.
3. Entertainment tax is a State tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Corporation tax is a Union tax in the shared pool and entertainment tax a State tax; agricultural income tax is a State tax (State List Entry 46).

s: Under Article 269, how are taxes on inter-State sale and consignment of goods, levied and collected by the Union, dealt with?
o: Shared as the GST Council advises
x: Article 269 taxes are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)
A. 268
B. 269
C. 270
D. 271
List-II (Arrangement)
1. Surcharge wholly for the Union
2. Levied by the Union, collected and kept by the States
3. Levied and collected by the Union, assigned to the States
4. Levied by the Union, shared with States on Finance Commission advice
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: 268 = stamp duties kept by States; 269 = assigned to States; 270 = shared pool; 271 = surcharge for the Union.

s: Under which Article is GST levied and collected by the Union on supplies in the course of inter-State trade?
x: Article 269A covers GST on inter-State trade (IGST); it is shared as Parliament provides on GST Council advice.

s: Agricultural income tax is levied by the States under which entry of the State List?
x: Agricultural income tax is a State tax under State List Entry 46; corporation tax is Union List Entry 85.

s: Which of the following duties is levied by the Union but collected and kept by the States under Article 268?
o: Excise on medicinal and toilet preparations
x: Article 268 covers stamp duties and excise on medicinal and toilet preparations; the States collect and keep them.

s: Which Article is associated with grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha?
x: Article 273 provided grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

s: What is the constitutional ceiling on taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments under Article 276?
x: Article 276 concerns taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments, subject to a ceiling of ₹2,500.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 292 deals with borrowing by the States.
2. Article 293 deals with borrowing by the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 292 deals with borrowing by the Union, while Article 293 deals with borrowing by the States.

s: Under which Article are the Contingency Fund of India and of the States provided?
x: Article 267 provides for the Contingency Fund; Article 266 covers the Consolidated Fund and Public Account.

s: Under which Article are the Consolidated Fund and the Public Account provided?
x: Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Fund and Public Account; 267 is the Contingency Fund.

s: Under Article 293(3), when does a State need the Centre's consent for fresh loans?
o: Any Union loan or guarantee is outstanding
It borrows for the first time
x: A State needs Centre's consent for fresh loans if any Union loan or guarantee is outstanding, and the Centre may attach conditions under 293(4).

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that 'No tax shall be levied except by authority of law'?
x: Article 265 says no tax shall be levied except by authority of law.

s: Since 2017, from which source may States borrow for infrastructure, only with the Centre's approval?
x: Since 2017 States may borrow from overseas bilateral agencies for infrastructure, but only with the Centre's approval.

s: Which Article requires the report of the Finance Commission to be laid before Parliament?
x: Article 280 sets up the Finance Commission; Article 281 lays its report before Parliament.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 293(3), a State needs the Centre's consent for fresh loans while any Union loan to it is outstanding.
2. Under Article 293(4), the Centre may attach conditions while giving such consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 293(3) requires the Centre's consent if a Union loan or guarantee is outstanding, and 293(4) lets the Centre attach conditions.

s: Under which Article are statutory grants-in-aid recommended by the Finance Commission made?
x: Article 275 grants are statutory and recommended by the Finance Commission; Article 282 allows discretionary grants for any public purpose.

s: Which Article is associated with grants for any public purpose chosen by the executive?
x: Article 282 covers grants for any public purpose; Article 275 grants are for States in need, ST welfare and Scheduled Areas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about grants to States?
o: Article 275 grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Plan grants continued after the Planning Commission was abolished in 2015
Article 282 grants are criticised as bypassing the Finance Commission
x: Plan grants ended when the Planning Commission was abolished in 2015.

s: On which fund are statutory grants-in-aid under Article 275 charged?
x: Article 275 grants, recommended by the Finance Commission, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; Article 282 grants are voted.

s: Article 275 grants-in-aid are specially meant for which of the following?
o: Welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
x: Article 275 statutory grants go to States in need, including for welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas.

s: What was the principal feature of the 'grand bargain' proposed by the 16th Finance Commission in relation to cesses?
o: All cesses would be transferred directly to local bodies
States would accept a smaller share of a larger pool if most cesses were merged into regular taxes
States would receive a larger share of a smaller pool without any change in cesses
States would impose all Union cesses within their territories
x: The proposal envisaged States taking a smaller share of a larger pool if the Centre merged most cesses into regular taxes.

s: The amount of cesses and surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax was at a decade high in which year and at what level?
x: Cesses and surcharges amounted to ₹13.5 per ₹100 of Central tax in 2021–22, described as a decade high. The estimate for 2025–26 was ₹11.

s: What was the approximate effective devolution to the States as a percentage of gross tax revenue, despite the headline 41% share of the divisible pool?
x: Because cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, the effective devolution was approximately 30–32% of gross tax revenue, lower than the headline 41% of the divisible pool.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270?
x: Cesses and surcharges lie outside the Article 270 divisible pool, so they are not shared with States.

s: Which of the following aggravates vertical fiscal imbalance between the Centre and States?
o: Cesses and surcharges kept outside the divisible pool
Removal of conditionalities on Centrally Sponsored Schemes
Retention of independent indirect taxes by States
x: Cesses and surcharges, loss of independent indirect taxes to GST, CSS conditionalities and weak State revenue all aggravate the imbalance.

s: What is the basic cause of vertical fiscal imbalance in India?
o: States have larger and more buoyant tax bases than the Union
The Union holds the larger and more buoyant tax bases such as corporation tax, income tax and most of GST
Local bodies collect most of the tax revenue in the country
The Finance Commission fixes the expenditure of States
x: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Union controls the larger, more buoyant tax bases (corporation tax, income tax, most of GST) while States carry heavy spending duties. A reverses the position, C is wrong because local bodies collect little, and the Finance Commission does not fix State expenditure (D).

s: Which government set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969), which advocated greater State autonomy?
x: The Tamil Nadu Government constituted the Rajamannar Committee in 1969; it argued for greater State autonomy and more resources.

s: During which period did the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations function?
x: The Sarkaria Commission sat during 1983–1988; the Rajamannar Committee dates to 1969 and the Punchhi Commission to 2007–2010.

s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council under Article 263 set up in 1990?
x: The Union-appointed Sarkaria Commission's recommendations led to the Inter-State Council in 1990.

s: Who chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations of 2007-10?
x: The Punchhi Commission (2007-10) was chaired by Justice M.M. Punchhi; Sarkaria was 1983-88.

s: Who chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations set up in 1983?
x: Justice R.S. Sarkaria chaired the 1983-88 Commission; its report led to the Inter-State Council (1990).

s: Revenue Deficit Grants to Andhra Pradesh are given under which Article of the Constitution?
x: AP receives Revenue Deficit Grants under Article 275, along with CSS funds, local body grants and SDLs raised through the RBI.

s: Through which institution does Andhra Pradesh raise its State Development Loans?
x: AP raises SDLs through the RBI.
